This page lists the spec and status fields of Addon, AddonObject and AddonRevision, each with its type, its limits and its description. The [Platform page](../../../platform/services/addons.md) explains the concept, and the `metadata` of every kind is [the same](../../common-definitions.md#objectmeta).

## Addon

::include[../../../../../api/types/v1alpha1/examples/addons/addon.yaml#addon]

| apiVersion | kind |
| --- | --- |
| `funcd.io/v1alpha1` | `Addon` |

### `Addon.spec`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `runtimes` | array of [`Addon.spec.runtimes[]`](#addonspecruntimes), required | The runtimes that the add-on ships, each an image and the workloads it serves. At most one entry runs the add-on's kind; an Addon whose entries run none adds no kind, and may gain one once. |

### `Addon.spec.runtimes[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attributes` | object, [`Addon.spec.runtimes[].attributes`](#addonspecruntimesattributes) | The entry's fields for its workloads: an Engine entry's kind, config, settings and engine fields. A Function or Job entry takes none. |
| `image` | string, matching `^[^:@\s]+(:[0-9]+/[^:@\s]+)?@sha256:[a-f0-9]{64}$` | The image, pinned by digest as &lt;repository&gt;@sha256:&lt;64 hex digits&gt;, from a registry that addons.registries lists, and pulled as an engine's. A registry taken out of that list stops no worker or engine, and refuses the Addon's next change. |
| `name` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | The runtime's name, which a Function's or a Job's spec.runtime names: a DNS label that is none of funcd's runtimes (nodejs22, python314, duckdb, rqlite), does not start with node or python, is no key of runtime.containerd.imageOverride, and that no other Addon ships. |
| `workloads` | array of string values, required, each one of `Function`, `Job`, `Engine` | What the image serves: Function and Job, which Functions and Jobs may name in spec.runtime, or Engine, alone, which runs one engine of the image per object of the entry's kind. |

### `Addon.spec.runtimes[].attributes`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `basePath` | string | The path under which the edge serves an object's engine, which the engine gets as it was called. It begins with /, does not end with / unless it is /, and holds no empty, . or .. segment. Empty is /. |
| `config` | any JSON value | The JSON Schema of the objects' spec.config, within funcd's contract profile: closed objects, and no $ref. funcd refuses an object whose config breaks it; an object stored before a change that its config breaks waits in Pending with ConfigInvalid, with no engine. |
| `env` | map of string to string | The engine's environment. Each value is a literal, or a single $&#123;&#123; &#125;&#125; expression over config, such as $&#123;&#123; config.issuer &#125;&#125;, which funcd checks against the config schema when the Addon is applied. A value that is not a string reaches the engine as its JSON; one that fails holds the object in Pending with EnvInvalid. |
| `kind` | string, matching `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]{1,62}$` | The namespaced kind that the entry runs: an upper-case letter, then 1 to 62 letters or digits. Its objects are served at /apis/funcd.io/v1alpha1/namespaces/&lt;namespace&gt;/&lt;plural&gt;, where the plural is the kind in lower case with an s. funcd refuses a kind that is its own, or whose plural is a path funcd serves or another Addon's plural, whatever the case. An Addon gains its kind once: it cannot change or go. |
| `port` | integer, 1 to 65535 | The port that the engine serves on, in its own network namespace; an Engine entry requires it. Only funcd reaches it. |
| `privatePaths` | array of string values | Paths under basePath that the edge answers with 404, however a caller spells them; funcd reaches them at the engine's own address. Each has basePath's form and lies under it. |
| `readiness` | object, [`Addon.spec.runtimes[].attributes.readiness`](#addonspecruntimesattributesreadiness) | How funcd learns that an object's engine is ready; an Engine entry requires it. |
| `restore` | object, [`Addon.spec.runtimes[].attributes.restore`](#addonspecruntimesattributesrestore) | How the engine loads a copy at its start, which an in-place Restore of an object puts in place. Unset, an object of the add-on cannot be restored. |
| `secretKeys` | array of string values | The keys of an object's bound Secrets that reach the engine's environment. A bound Secret's other keys do not. |
| `settings` | array of [`Addon.spec.runtimes[].attributes.settings[]`](#addonspecruntimesattributessettings) | Kinds of settings objects that the add-on adds beside kind. An object of one runs no engine: the kind's Function applies the objects of each target through the target's engine. |
| `snapshot` | object, [`Addon.spec.runtimes[].attributes.snapshot`](#addonspecruntimesattributessnapshot) | Where the engine writes its own consistent copies, which a Backup of an object copies. Unset, a Backup that names an object of the add-on fails with reason NoSnapshot, and a resourceGroup scope leaves the add-on's objects out. |
| `storage` | object, [`Addon.spec.runtimes[].attributes.storage`](#addonspecruntimesattributesstorage) | A directory that outlives each object's engine, kept across a replaced engine and funcd's restarts. Unset, the engine keeps nothing. |

### `Addon.spec.runtimes[].attributes.readiness`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string, required | The path that funcd sends GET to on the engine's port. The object turns Ready once it answers 200. |

### `Addon.spec.runtimes[].attributes.restore`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | map of string to string | The environment of the start that loads the copy, laid over env. Each value is a literal, or a single $&#123;&#123; &#125;&#125; expression over config and restore, such as $&#123;&#123; "file:" + restore.file &#125;&#125;: restore.file is the copy's path in the engine. |
| `path` | string, required | The folder in the engine where funcd puts the copy that the next start loads: under storage.path, and neither snapshot.path nor inside it. funcd empties it before it writes the copy, and removes the copy once the engine that loaded it is Ready. |
| `timeout` | string, a duration: whole numbers with the units h, m, s and ms, largest unit first (10m, 1h30m, 500ms) | How long an in-place Restore waits for the engine to load the copy and start again without restore.env, from 1s to 1h; unset is 10m. Past it, the Restore fails with reason RestoreTimedOut and the namespace stays held. |

## AddonObject

::include[../../../../../api/types/v1alpha1/examples/addons/addonobject.yaml#addonobject]

| apiVersion | kind |

| `funcd.io/v1alpha1` | `AddonObject` |

### `AddonObject.spec`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bindings` | object, [`AddonObject.spec.bindings`](#addonobjectspecbindings) | What the object's engine uses. |
| `config` | any JSON value | The object's settings, which the schema in its Addon's spec.config checks. Unset is an empty object. |
| `deletion` | string, one of `retain`, `delete` | What becomes of the engine's storage once the object is deleted and its engine is gone: retain, the default, moves it into the quarantine for storage.quarantineRetention, from which it comes back by hand with funcd stopped; delete removes it. A new object of the same name starts empty either way. |
| `functions` | array of [`AddonObject.spec.functions[]`](#addonobjectspecfunctions) | The object's own Function for a settings kind of its Addon, in place of the kind's function.ref, so each copy of an App template applies its own objects. A settings object names none. |
| `ingress` | object, [`AddonObject.spec.ingress`](#addonobjectspecingress) | Exposes the engine at the edge, on ingress.host under its Addon's basePath, while the object is Ready. Its own ingress.auth alone decides the stance, open when unset; ingress.path and the authenticated mode are refused. |
| `kind` | string | The add-on's kind, which funcd sets from the path the object is written at. |
| `resources` | object, [`AddonObject.spec.resources`](#addonobjectspecresources) | The cpu and memory of the object's engine. An empty cpu or memory sets no limit, and a change replaces the running engine. |

### `AddonObject.spec.bindings`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `secret` | array of string values, each a DNS-1123 label | Secrets of the namespace whose keys, those that the Addon's spec.secretKeys lists, reach the engine's environment. funcd asks Cedar, as the object, for secret::read on each: a missing Secret holds the object in Pending with SecretNotFound, and a forbidden one with BindingResolveFailed. A changed value replaces the engine. |

### `AddonObject.spec.functions[]`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | string, required | A settings kind of the object's Addon, named once. |
| `ref` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | A Function of the object's namespace that binds the object in its bindings.addon, which funcd calls with the object's settings objects of the kind. In an App, a Function the App declares. |

### `AddonObject.spec.ingress`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `auth` | object, [`AddonObject.spec.ingress.auth`](#addonobjectspecingressauth) | How the edge checks callers at the resource's own address; unset, the namespace's spec.edgeDefaults.auth decides, else open. A Lake refuses it, since the Lake gateway checks each caller. |
| `enabled` | boolean | Turns the resource's own address on or off. Unset, it is on unless the namespace's spec.defaultExposure is explicit; a Lake's address is on only when this is true. |
| `host` | string | The exact host of the resource's own address. Empty is the namespace's host, &lt;namespace&gt;.&lt;server.baseDomain&gt;, or, in the default namespace, any host that no other namespace reserves. |
| `path` | string | The edge path of the resource's own address, which begins with / and does not end with / unless it is /. Empty is / when host is set, else /function/&lt;name&gt;, /site/&lt;name&gt; or /lake/&lt;name&gt; by kind. |

### `AddonObject.spec.ingress.auth`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `mode` | string, one of `""`, `authenticated`, `open`, `oidc` | How the edge checks callers. authenticated requires a bearer token, or an X-Api-Key header, of an identity that RBAC lets get Functions in the namespace: 401 without a valid one, 403 when it may not; while server.auth.edge is off, every caller gets 401. open lets anonymous callers in. oidc signs callers in with the OIDCProvider that provider names, and passes the signed-in user to the code behind it in the X-Funcd-Principal headers. Empty takes the enclosing stance, if any, else the namespace's spec.edgeDefaults.auth.mode, else open. |
| `provider` | string, a DNS-1123 label | With mode oidc, the OIDCProvider of the namespace that signs callers in; required with oidc and refused with another mode. |
| `unauthenticated` | string, one of `""`, `redirect`, `401`, `allow` | With mode oidc, what a call that is not signed in gets: redirect, the default, sends a GET or HEAD navigation to the provider with 302 and gives any other call 401; 401 gives every such call 401; allow passes every call, with no principal. Refused with another mode. |

### `AddonObject.spec.resources`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cpu` | string | The CPU cap of the worker or engine it sizes, as a number of cores of at least 0.01, such as 0.5 or 2. Empty takes the default of the resource that declares it, or no cap when there is none. Only the containerd runtime enforces it. |
| `memory` | string | The memory cap of the worker or engine it sizes, such as 256Mi or 4GiB: 1 to 15 digits and an optional binary unit, Ki, Mi, Gi or Ti, with or without a B, above zero. Empty takes the default of the resource that declares it, or no cap when there is none. Only the containerd runtime enforces it, and there a worker that uses more memory than the cap is killed. |

### `AddonObject.status`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `addonRevision` | string, a DNS-1123 label | The AddonRevision whose spec the engine runs. A newer revision of the Addon moves no object: an edit of the object moves it to the Addon's current revision, and for an App's part, the App's revision moves it. |
| `address` | string | The engine's own address, its host and port, which only funcd reaches. |
| `appRevision` | string, a DNS-1123 label | For an App's part, the AppRevision whose record for its kind it pins: the App's latest revision once that one is applied. A part moves forward only. |
| `conditions` | array of [Condition](../../common-definitions.md#condition) | The conditions that explain the phase. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer | The generation of the spec that funcd last acted on. |
| `phase` | string, one of `Pending`, `Deploying`, `Ready`, `Idle`, `Degraded`, `Failed`, `Terminating` | Where the object is in its lifecycle. |
| `restore` | object, [`AddonObject.status.restore`](#addonobjectstatusrestore) | The in-place Restore whose copy the engine loads: it goes once an engine started without restore.env is Ready, or once that Restore has failed or is gone. While it stands, the namespace is held. |

### `AddonObject.status.restore`

| Field | Type and limits | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | string, required | The copy's file name in the Addon's restore.path. |
| `restore` | string, required, a DNS-1123 label | The Restore that placed the copy. |
| `state` | string, required, one of `Loading`, `Loaded` | Loading while the engine starts with restore.env to load the copy; Loaded once the copy is gone, while the engine starts again without restore.env. |

## Handler API

The methods a handler calls on its context's clients, in each language funcd ships a shim for.

### `ctx.addon`

#### TypeScript

The add-on objects that the function binds, by alias: fetch calls an object's engine through funcd, which serves only the paths that the object's edge entry serves.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `fetch(alias: string, path: string, init?: RequestInit): Promise<Response>` | Sends an HTTP request to the engine of the add-on object that the function binds under alias, through funcd, and returns the engine's answer as a Response, whatever its status; funcd follows no redirect. path starts with "/" and may carry a query, and init sets the method, the headers and the body, as for the global fetch. Rejects with an AddonError when funcd refuses the call: 403 for an alias the function does not bind or a call a Policy forbids, 404 for a path the object's edge entry does not serve, 413 for a request or an answer body over addons.callPayloadLimit, 1 MiB by default, and 503 while the object is not Ready, while its namespace is held (with retryAfter), or when the engine does not answer within addons.callTimeout, 10 seconds by default. |

Each method here that calls funcd can also fail with the status 500 and the problem type `urn:funcd:problem:internal`, when funcd meets an error that it did not expect; funcd logs its cause.

When funcd refuses a call, the method fails with an error that holds funcd's status and problem type. This table gives them for each method, with when each happens and what to do.

| Method | Status | Problem type | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fetch` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | The Function binds no add-on object under the alias. | Call an alias of spec.bindings.addon, or add it there. |
| `fetch` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | Cedar denies the Function addon::call on the object, as when a Policy forbids it. | Ask the operator to lift the forbid. |
| `fetch` | 404 | `urn:funcd:problem:not-found` | The path names no alias, or the object's edge entry would refuse it: outside its Addon's basePath, under one of its privatePaths, or with a .. segment. | Call a path under the Addon's basePath that it does not keep private. |
| `fetch` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The request's body is larger than the local API takes for the call. | Send a smaller body. |
| `fetch` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The engine's answer body is larger than addons.callPayloadLimit. | Ask for less, or ask the operator to raise addons.callPayloadLimit. |
| `fetch` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The caller's namespace is held while a Restore loads its data. | Retry after the Retry-After seconds. |
| `fetch` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The add-on object is not Ready, has no engine address yet, or its engine refused the connection. | Wait until the object is Ready, then retry. |
| `fetch` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The engine did not answer within addons.callTimeout. | Retry, or ask the operator to raise addons.callTimeout. |
| `fetch` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The engine's answer ended before its body did. | Retry. |

#### Python

The add-on objects that the function binds, by alias: ``fetch`` sends an HTTP request to an object's engine through funcd, which checks the binding and the path as the object's edge entry does, and returns the engine's answer whatever its status.

| Method | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `fetch(alias: str, path: str, method: str = 'GET', headers: dict[str, str] \| None = None, body: bytes \| None = None) -> AddonResponse` | Sends an HTTP request to the engine of the add-on object that the function binds under ``alias``, through funcd, and returns the engine's answer whatever its status; funcd follows no redirect. ``path`` starts with ``/`` and may carry a query, and ``method``, ``headers`` and ``body`` make the rest of the request. Raises ``RuntimeError`` with funcd's problem when funcd refuses the call: 403 for an alias the function does not bind or a call a Policy forbids, 404 for a path the object's edge entry does not serve, 413 for a request or an answer body over ``addons.callPayloadLimit``, 1 MiB by default, and 503 while the object is not Ready, while its namespace is held (with its ``Retry-After``), or when the engine does not answer within ``addons.callTimeout``, 10 seconds by default. |

Each method here that calls funcd can also fail with the status 500 and the problem type `urn:funcd:problem:internal`, when funcd meets an error that it did not expect; funcd logs its cause.

When funcd refuses a call, the method fails with an error that holds funcd's status and problem type. This table gives them for each method, with when each happens and what to do.

| Method | Status | Problem type | When | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fetch` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | The Function binds no add-on object under the alias. | Call an alias of spec.bindings.addon, or add it there. |
| `fetch` | 403 | `urn:funcd:problem:forbidden` | Cedar denies the Function addon::call on the object, as when a Policy forbids it. | Ask the operator to lift the forbid. |
| `fetch` | 404 | `urn:funcd:problem:not-found` | The path names no alias, or the object's edge entry would refuse it: outside its Addon's basePath, under one of its privatePaths, or with a .. segment. | Call a path under the Addon's basePath that it does not keep private. |
| `fetch` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The request's body is larger than the local API takes for the call. | Send a smaller body. |
| `fetch` | 413 | `urn:funcd:problem:payload-too-large` | The engine's answer body is larger than addons.callPayloadLimit. | Ask for less, or ask the operator to raise addons.callPayloadLimit. |
| `fetch` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The caller's namespace is held while a Restore loads its data. | Retry after the Retry-After seconds. |
| `fetch` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The add-on object is not Ready, has no engine address yet, or its engine refused the connection. | Wait until the object is Ready, then retry. |
| `fetch` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The engine did not answer within addons.callTimeout. | Retry, or ask the operator to raise addons.callTimeout. |
| `fetch` | 503 | `urn:funcd:problem:unavailable` | The engine's answer ended before its body did. | Retry. |
